clauses.clause: Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes.
clauses.note: Students independently write responses (Parts III and IV) about major events and central message.

verdicts.evidence:
- Tell students that now they are going to write what they know about the major events and central message of Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky, just as they did in Lessons 9 and 11.
- Distribute prepared clipboards with Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky response sheets and pencils and follow the same routine established in Lessons 9 and 11 to complete Parts III and IV.
- Circulate to support students as they write. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Story Elements board, Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts).
verdicts.rationale: Students interpret the text to explain and discuss the central message and then construct written responses demonstrating their understanding of key concepts and events.

clauses.clause: Refer to parts of texts when supporting an idea, answer, or opinion.
clauses.note: Students cite what they heard and saw in the text/illustrations to explain key events.

clauses.clause: Explore various sources of information, including print, digital, and personal communication.
clauses.note: Lesson focuses on a single literary text; no exploration of multiple sources to make connections.

verdicts.evidence:
Ask:
'What did you hear that helped you understand the important events from the beginning of the story?' (Sun wants Water to visit his and Moon's house, but Water says the house is too small for all of his people. Sun and Moon decide to build a larger house.)
'What did you see in the illustrations that helped you understand the beginning of the story?' (Sun had a small house and was talking with Water. Sun and Moon started building a bigger house.)
verdicts.rationale: Students reference specific parts of the text and illustrations to support their answers, but they do not explore multiple sources of information.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Reference parts of texts to address a specific topic or question and explore various sources of information to make connections across a broad range of topics.
